region.text: Kalinga: Uttara Kalinga (Srikakulam, Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada districts) and Kalinganagara (Mukhalingam)

ledger.note: 1078: Anantavarman Chodaganga becomes king and the Ganga empire begins. 'Anantavarman Chodaganga Succeeded his father in 1078 AD' (ruler list c. 1077); 'emperor from 1078 until his death in 1150' (Chodaganga page). The dynasty itself is dated to 493 on the infobox and the Cholas had brought the Ganga kingdom under their rule in the 11th century. The core is the Kalinga proper of the page (Srikakulam, Ganjam, Gajapati and Rayagada districts), a reading.

region.text: the Visakhapatnam district, lost 'for a while'

ledger.note: 1078: the Cholas take the Visakhapatnam district. 'In the initial years of his reign his kingdom was attacked by the Cholas of the south and for a while Chodaganga lost to them a part of his kingdom comprising the Visakhapatnam district but he did not lose heart and gradually recovered his lost territories' (Eastern Ganga page). The page gives no year for the attack, so 1078, the first year of the reign, is used; the recovery is the 1118 event below (the earlier version left out the recovery clause). Kulottunga's Visakhapatnam harbour was renamed Kulottungacolapattanam (Kulottunga page, undated).

region.text: Kalinga proper including the capital Kalinganagara

ledger.note: c. 1102: the Cholas take Kalinga proper in Kulottunga's second Kalinga war. 'The first war seems to have occurred before 1096'; 'The second invasion took place a few years later, sometime before the 33rd year of the king's reign', led by his general Karunakara Tondaiman, who 'defeated the Kalinga ruler Anantavarman Chodaganga' (Kulottunga reigned from 1070, so the 33rd regnal year is c. 1102; the page gives a bound, not a date). The page attests Chola rule over 'some parts of Kalinga (proper) including the capital Kalinganagara' only in his 45th regnal year, 'c. 1115 CE', which the earlier version used as the date of the loss; 1115 is the attestation, not the conquest (repair of 2026-10-19).

region.text: Utkala (Northern Odisha): the Odisha province without the southern Kalinga districts held since 1078

ledger.note: 1118: Utkala is Ganga. 'Anantavarman also captured Utkala (Northern Odisha) from the Somavamshi Kings' (Eastern Ganga page, no year); the Sindurapura grant, 'Saka year 1040 (1118 CE)', says he 'had sovereignty over entire of the whole Utkala', and the Chodaganga page puts the incorporation 'with the decline of the Somavamshis' (undated, so the conquest lies before 1118; 1118 is the attestation). He 'shifted the capital to Chaudwar Cuttack' after defeating the last Kesari king (Madalapanji). Region corrected in the repair of 2026-10-19: northern and central Odisha only (the Odisha province minus the Brahmapur disc and an 80 km disc at Rayagada, both Kalinga proper since 1078); the first version gave all of Odisha, which put Utkala on the map 40 years early. Cliopatria's shape holds Odisha from 1056; the 1118 keyframe takes the 367 of these cells that lie in its outline.

c. 1118 (bridge): Chodaganga recovers the Visakhapatnam district. 'for a while Chodaganga lost to them a part of his kingdom comprising the Visakhapatnam district but he did not lose heart and gradually recovered his lost territories' (Eastern Ganga page, no year). The Chodaganga page has his 'empire extended to river Godavari in the south', and 1118 is the year it has him take Vengi north of the Godavari after Kulottunga's death, so the district was Ganga by then; confidence 1. Added in the repair of 2026-10-19; chola-empire has no matching loss.

region.text: the part of Vengi lying north of the Godavari

ledger.note: c. 1118-1122 (bridge): Chodaganga takes the north of Vengi. 'It seems that Chodaganga saw this as an advantage and conquered the part of Vengi lying north to river Godavari', where 'this' is the Chola weakness at Kulottunga's death, which the Chodaganga page dates to 1118 ('After the death of Kulottunga in 1118 AD vengi came under the rule of Vikramchola'); the Kulottunga page has his reign to 1122 and 'the northern half of the Vengi kingdom seems to have slipped from his hands' late in it. He 'was failed to conquer the whole of Vengi'. 1118 is used (confidence 1; moved from c. 1100 in the repair of 2026-10-19). Reconciliation with the Western Chalukyas: chola-empire /ledger/32 and western-chalukya-empire /ledger/24 give the whole of Vengi to the Western Chalukyas from c. 1118; the Ganga land here is only the strip north of the Godavari, which no page marks off from the Chalukya-held part. The counterpart stays chola-empire because the Chodaganga page names Vikrama Chola, not the Chalukyas; the pages disagree and this is not settled.

c. 1126 (bridge): Kalinga proper is Ganga again. No page dates the recovery from the Cholas; the Chodaganga page has an empire from the Ganga to the Godavari at his death in 1150 and the Kulottunga page has the northern half of Vengi 'seems to have slipped' from Chola hands late in the reign; Cliopatria shrinks the Chola shape in 1126. Confidence 1. The Visakhapatnam district is the separate event of 1118; the Kalinga loss it reverses is dated c. 1102 (repair of 2026-10-19).

c. 1150 (bridge): Kamarnava VII fights for Sambalpur. 'During his reign he fought with the Kalachuris of Ratnapura for the possession of the Sambalpur- Bolangir Tract but was unsuccessful' (ruler list c. 1150-1156). The page gives no year and no battle, so his reign is used (confidence 1). No land changes hands. This pair replaces the earlier c. 1152 'gain' of Sambalpur, which the page contradicts (repair of 2026-10-19).

region.text: the cells that leave Cliopatria's shape in 1152, without the Visakhapatnam district

ledger.note: 1152: Cliopatria's shape loses 104 cells; 15 of them lie in the Visakhapatnam district (by the gazetteer test), which the dossier keeps from its recovery in 1118, leaving 89 cells in the south-west of the old shape. They have no page: confidence 1.

region.text: the Vengi strip north of the Godavari

ledger.note: 1152 (bridge): the Vengi strip leaves the shape. region.text: the Sambalpur-Bolangir Tract (the 27 cells that Cliopatria adds at Sambalpur in 1152)

ledger.note: 1211 (earliest year of the reign; bridge): Anangabhima III takes the Sambalpur tract. 'In his reign he conquered the west part of Odisha known as the Sambalpur- Bolangir Tract' 'which was in hold of the Kalachuris of Ratnapura' (the page gives his reign as 1211-1238 and no year for the conquest). Cliopatria's shape carries the 27 Sambalpur cells from 1152, 59 years early; the keyframe correction removes them until this event. Confidence 1; Bolangir is not drawn separately.

1243: Narasimha I's army moves on Bengal. 'Forces moved toward Bengal in 1242-1243 CE'; 'In 1244 CE, the victorious Odia forces again seized two provinces of Varendra and Rarh' and 'surrounded the Lakhnauti fort'. The EG page has him 'advanced to Varendra as far as Lakhnawati in 1245'.

1244: Odia forces occupy Rarh and Gauda. 'the victorious Odia forces again seized two provinces of Varendra and Rarh' and 'Rarh and Gauda remained occupied by the Odia forces and the northern frontiers of Kalinga ... expanded after these expeditions ... while Varendra remained under secluded Mamluk authority' (Tughril Tughan launched a counterattack by 1244 at the frontier fort of Katasin, Contai). The page calls the land occupied, not annexed, so it is an occupation (hatched) and not a gain; changed from a gain in the repair of 2026-10-19. Cliopatria's Mamluk shape holds 258 of the 311 West Bengal cells in 1244.

1247: Delhi sends a new governor. 'In 1247 CE, a new governor, Ikhtiyar-ud-Din Yuzbak, was appointed to free Bengal from Odia forces. Paramardi Dev was killed in the fighting at Mandarana or Umurdan.' The page does not say who held Rarh afterwards (confidence 1 for the end).

1247 (bridge): the occupation of Rarh and Gauda is taken to end. 'In 1247 CE, an able new Muslim military commander, lkhtiyar-ud-Din Yuzbak, was appointed as the governor of Bengal' (the contest of 1243-1247 ends the same year). The page does not say when the Odia occupation ended; it adds that the Muslims 'halted their progress into Odisha fearing retaliation' and that there is 'no record of any direct Muslim invasion of Odishan territory for at least the next hundred years'. Cliopatria's Ganga shapes from 1260 have no West Bengal cell, so the end lies between 1247 and 1260; 1247 is a bridge (confidence 1).

1358: the Tughlaq invasion ends. No territorial result on the page; the Musunuri Nayaks 'defeated the Odishan powers in 1356' (no place).

1358: the Ganga king pays tribute to Delhi. 'the sultan of Delhi, Firuz Shah Tughlaq, invaded Odisha between 1353 and 1358, and levied tribute on the Ganga king' (the page gives no year for the levy; the end of the invasion is used). Tribute only: no land changes hands (see the contest of 1353-1358). Written from the tribute-payer's side as the 2026-10-19 review asked; the schema describes vassal events from the suzerain's side, so tughlaq-dynasty (sa-04) should carry the mirror with this state as its counterpart.

1359 (bridge): the tint ends. The page records one levy and no continuing obligation, and says the Musunuri Nayaks 'defeated the Odishan powers in 1356' (no place); Cliopatria draws the Ganga shape as independent to 1351. One year is the shortest tint the grammar allows (confidence 1).

region.text: the Ganga realm of the last years

ledger.note: 1434: Kapilendra ends the Eastern Gangas. 'The rule of the dynasty came to an end under the reign of King Bhanudeva IV (c. 1414-34)' (list: Bhanu Deva IV 1425-1434, 'last ruler of dynasty'); 'his minister Kapilendra usurped the throne and founded the Suryavamsha dynasty in 1434-35'.

wars.name: Ganga-Chola wars over Kalinga and Vengi
wars.outcome: The Cholas take the Visakhapatnam district early in Chodaganga's reign ('gradually recovered', c. 1118); Kulottunga I's two Kalinga wars (the second, c. 1102, led by Karunakara Tondaiman) leave parts of Kalinga proper including Kalinganagara Chola, attested c. 1115 and bridged to the Ganga return c. 1126; Chodaganga takes Vengi north of the Godavari after Kulottunga's death (1118).
wars.note: Dates: the first war 'before 1096', the second 'before the 33rd year' of the reign (c. 1102), Chola rule attested in the 45th regnal year (c. 1115); the EG page has the Cholas take Visakhapatnam in the 'initial years' of Chodaganga's reign. Zones as in the ledger.

wars.name: Ganga-Kalachuri conflict for Kosala and Sambalpur
wars.outcome: A 'long conflict for the control of the Trikalinga and Kosala regions': Ratnadeva II (1120-1135) 'repulsed an invasion by Anantavarman Chodaganga'; Kamarnava VII fought for the Sambalpur-Bolangir Tract 'but was unsuccessful'; Anangabhima III 'conquered the west part of Odisha known as the Sambalpur- Bolangir Tract' in his reign (1211-1238) and may have beaten Pratapamalla (1200-1225).
wars.note: No year for any invasion; the Ratnapura dynasty survives to the 18th century.

wars.name: Khalji attack on Jajnagar
wars.outcome: 'In 1205 Bakhtiyar Khalji sent Muhammad Sheran Khalji with a portion of his forces towards Jajnagar'; 'the first invasion of Muslims in Odisha was unsuccessful'.

wars.name: Narasimha I's Bengal campaign
wars.outcome: The Odia army seizes Rarh and Varendra in 1244, besieges Lakhnauti, is counter-attacked by Tughril Tughan Khan near Katasin (Contai) and is pushed back after Yuzbak's appointment in 1247; Rarh and Gauda 'stayed under Odia control' according to the page while Varendra remained under Mamluk authority.
wars.note: The page also has the Kakatiya king Ganapati 'humbled' and territorial disputes near the Godavari.

wars.name: Firuz Shah Tughlaq's invasion of Odisha
wars.outcome: Tribute was levied on the Ganga king; no territorial result is on the page.
wars.note: 'the sultan of Delhi, Firuz Shah Tughlaq, invaded Odisha between 1353 and 1358, and levied tribute on the Ganga king' (Eastern Ganga page); recorded as a vassal_start in 1358 and a bridged vassal_end in 1359.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on any page; Bengal and Vengi frontiers were fought over each decade and the interior is given only as district names.

notes:
WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'Eastern Ganga Kingdom' (1056-1351, 7 shapes of 522-755 cells: Odisha 455-537, Andhra Pradesh 25-66, Chhattisgarh 17-102, Jharkhand 10-48, no West Bengal) draws the Odisha state from 1056 and stops in 1351. The Eastern Ganga page dates the dynasty to 493 (Indravarman I), has the Cholas rule the Ganga kingdom in the 11th century, begins Chodaganga's empire in 1078 and ends the dynasty in 1434 (Kapilendra, 1434-35). The dossier is drawn from 1078 to 1434: the Cliopatria shapes of 1056-1077 are not drawn, and 1352-1434 carries the 1344 outline (confidence 1) because Cliopatria has no Odisha row afterwards. START/END therefore differ from Cliopatria by 22 years at the start and 83 at the end. Pre-1078 history (the Eastern Gangas of Kalinganagara, 493-1078) is not covered by any dossier; an earlier Ganga dossier would be a gap-filler's job.

PAGES (budget 5): Eastern Ganga dynasty (opened three times for three questions), Chodaganga, Narasingha Deva I, Kulottunga I, Ratnapura Kalachuris. Disagreements and silences: (1) the Chola attack on the Visakhapatnam district is 'initial years' of 1078 (no year; 1078 used); (2) Utkala is 'with the decline of the Somavamshis' (undated) and attested by a grant of 1118; (3) the extent 'from the Ganges to the Godavari' and 'Midnapore in the north' (Chodaganga page) has no cell in Cliopatria's shape for Bengal or the Godavari: not drawn, only events at confidence 1-2; (4) 1244 versus 1245 for Narasimha I at Lakhnauti, and 'Rarh and Gauda stayed under Odia control' while Delhi sent Yuzbak in 1247: the end of the contest is confidence 1; (5) 1260: no page for the +238 cells (Chhattisgarh was the Ratnapura Kalachuris' Kosala); (6) 'Bhanudeva IV (c. 1414-34)' in the body against 1425-1434 in the list; (7) Kamarnava VII/'Kamarnnava Deva' and the other names differ between body and list.

COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT DOSSIERS: Somavamshi dynasty (Kosala/Utkala, 10th-11th c.), Kalachuri of Ratnapura (suggested slug kalachuri-of-ratnapura), suryavamsha-dynasty (Kapilendra's Gajapati state from 1434), and the Delhi governors of Bengal (Tughril Tughan Khan, Yuzbak) under mamluk-dynasty. Gazetteer names wanted: Kalinga (proper), Utkala, Kalinganagara/Mukhalingam, Sambalpur is present, Srikakulam, Ganjam, Rarh/Radha, Varendra, Gauda, Lakhnauti, Vengi.

REPAIR OF 2026-10-19 (reviewer findings, all re-read from the pages). (1) Keyframe 1056 split: 1078-1101 Kalinga proper, new keyframes 1102 (Kalinganagara Chola), 1118 (Utkala, Visakhapatnam, north Vengi added), 1126 (Kalinganagara back), and the Utkala gain region is now northern and central Odisha only. The Kalinga proper region adds an 80 km disc at Rayagada (the page's district list; not in the gazetteer) to the Brahmapur disc. (2) Visakhapatnam: recovery gain 1118 (confidence 1; the page says only 'gradually recovered'); the district is added back to every shape from 1118 (Cliopatria drops it in 1152 and restores it in 1260). (3) Sambalpur: the page contradicts the 1152 gain (Kamarnava VII 'was unsuccessful'); it is now a contest pair 1150-1156 and a gain by Anangabhima III in 1211 (the page's reign 1211-1238, confidence 1), with the 27 cells removed from the 1152-1210 shape. This goes beyond the reviewer's suggestion (remove the cells or keep them Kalachuri) because the same page dates the real conquest to Anangabhima III. (4) Vengi: moved from c. 1100 to 1118; the Western Chalukya overlap is documented, not resolved, and the counterpart stays chola-empire (Chodaganga page: Vengi 'came under the rule of Vikramchola'); the strip leaves the shape in 1152 (bridge).
